jobs.title: Senior HR Business Partner
jobs.description:
We're building the nervous system for the next generation of satellites.

ReOrbit designs software-first, intelligent satellites that talk to each other in orbit not just fly next to each other. We're a Helsinki-headquartered deep-tech scale-up with teams in Bangalore, Bristol, and Bariloche, and we're growing fast across all four.

That growth is exactly the problem we need you to help us solve.

The role

We need a Senior HRBP who can build the people foundations for a company that's scaling across four countries at once without slowing us down with process for process's sake. You'll be the person leadership turns to when a reorg needs designing or a manager needs coaching through a hard conversation.

This isn't a maintain-the-status-quo HR role. It's a build-it role.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

• Shaping how we're organized. Partner directly with leadership on org design and workforce planning as we scale — not after the fact, but as part of the decision-making.
• Keeping us legally sound across borders. Own employment law compliance in Finland and beyond, from contracts to labor relations, working hands-on with legal counsel where it matters.
• Making managers better. Coach leaders through complex people situations and build performance systems that actually help people grow, not just tick a review-cycle box.
• Building the playbook. Create HR policies and processes that are lean enough for a scale-up but solid enough to hold up as we grow — across four very different regulatory environments.
• Making "one company" real. Drive consistency in how we hire, pay, relocate, and support people across Finland, India, UK, and Argentina, even as local rules differ.
• Running the programs that keep people here. Lead engagement, retention, and leadership development efforts with a genuinely people-first approach.

What You Bring

• 10+ years of HR experience with substantial experience as HRBP or senior HR professional.
• Proven experience in scale up or startup environments (tech, engineering, deep tech strongly preferred).
• Strong expertise in organizational design, structuring teams and guiding managers through change.
• Solid understanding of employment law (Finland/EU) and compliance with hands on experience collaborating with legal counsel on HR matters.
• Experience building and implementing performance management and development systems in scaling organizations.
• Experience supporting international teams and building robust cross country HR foundations.
• High level of maturity, autonomy and stakeholder skills to advise and influence leadership directly.

Working at ReOrbit

At ReOrbit, we are focused on building a strong team as we believe nothing can be accomplished without innovative, humble and curious minds working together on a common goal. We’re all about fostering an inclusive, dynamic environment where equality and diversity are our strength.

We offer

• Challenging but rewarding environment – you will thrive if you are always reflecting on how to make things better. Your ideas will be heard.
• Ambitious and supportive network of people, who are motivated to change the space industry, bringing expertise from both classic and new space .
• Benefits such as lunch vouchers, events, parties, occupational health care and additional health insurance - but most importantly a possibility to be a part of a unique and diverse team, connected by similar mindset and sense of humor.
• We support relocation and integration into Finnish society.

If you'd rather inherit a finished HR machine than build one, this probably isn't your role. If the idea of designing how a deep-tech company scales gets you excited — we want to hear from you.

Apply soon — we're moving fast and can't wait to meet you.

jobs.title: Compensation Analyst
jobs.description:
Role: Compensation Analyst
Location: London (Hybrid, minimum 3 days/week in office)
Salary: £70,000 plus strong discretionary bonus and excellent benefits

Middlemore have been retained by an international PLC in the financial and professional services sector to recruit a highly skilled Compensation Analyst, working with the Director of Group Compensation and Benefits.

The role offers an exceptional opportunity for professional development – whether that be into the wider world of global Total Reward, or deepening your expertise as a Compensation Analyst; there is no ceiling in this position.

As the sole Compensation Analyst, you’ll play a critical role in delivering everything from regulatory reporting to supporting annual comp reviews – this role gives you genuine autonomy and ownership from day one, benefiting from the support and development of an experienced Global Director.

Key responsibilities include, but aren’t limited to:

• Regulatory reporting: Gender Pay Gap, CEO Pay Ratio, FCA Remuneration submissions – prior experience of this will be required
• Salary benchmarking
• Full annual compensation review cycle: data reconciliation, UAT, bonus apportionments, stakeholder distribution
• Share scheme administration: LTIP, SAYE, executive options, monthly share tracking
• Producing remuneration reports for UK statutory directors
• Payroll costings and business insurance data
• Ad hoc HR projects and reporting to senior leadership, including CFO and CEO

What's in It for You

The organisation wants to be clear that there is no ceiling in this position and there are a number of different professional development opportunities on offer: either pivoting into broader Total Compensation, or deepening your expertise as a Compensation Analyst and developing the sophistication of the offering globally across the PLC.

• Career optionality: stay technical or develop towards business partnering
• Dynamic, acquisitive business with live projects beyond BAU
• Support from an established Director who has grown through this role
• A sophisticated business which encourages curiosity, experimentation, new ways of working and creativity

What We're Looking For

• 5–10+ years' experience as a Compensation Analyst
• Expert-level Excel (pivots, VLOOKUPs, macros, complex workbooks)
• Experience with systems such as SuccessFactors, ResourceLink and/or Payscale Curo would be desirable, but is not required
• Able to deliver the full technical comp remit unsupported from day one
• Curious, problem-solving mindset, not just transactional

If this role is of interest, please apply through this advert.

jobs.title: Global HR Business Partner
jobs.description:
Ready to help build a better future for generations to come?

In an ever-changing, fast paced world, we owe it to ourselves and our future generations to live life responsibly. At ROCKWOOL, we work relentlessly to enrich modern living through our innovative stone wool solutions.

Join us and make a difference!

The Opportunity

ROCKWOOL is seeking a highly experienced Global HR Business Partner to join our headquarters in Hedehusene, Denmark. This is a rare and exciting opportunity to contribute to a well-established organization with ambitious strategic plans, where HR plays a pivotal role in shaping success.

Your future team

You will join a collaborative and supportive HR team and contribute to an organization with a strong commitment to sustainability and environmental impact. You will work closely with different colleagues, across borders and HR CoEs, and have the chance to take ownership of strategic initiatives that directly impact the development of key global functions.

What You Will Be Doing

You will partner with two key global functions—Group Technology and Project Execution—which are VP areas and part of Group Operations & Technology (GOT). Group Technology is the engineering backbone of ROCKWOOL, with specialized engineers responsible for delivering technical solutions. Project Execution with highly experienced project leaders is responsible for executing complex and critical projects, such as renovating and building new factories globally.

As the company continues to evolve to be future fit, we require a forward-thinking senior HR Business Partner who can act as a trusted advisor to the business, translating strategy into people priorities and executing them with precision.

Trusted advisor

• Being trusted advisor and partner with the VP and their leadership team on strategy, organization, capability, leadership, culture, and performance priorities.

Talent Management & leadership development

• Identify and analyse current skills versus future needs and define plans to bridge gaps through hiring, development, and deployment.
• Manage succession planning by identifying high-potential employees and preparing them for critical roles.
• Support leadership continuity and capability-building across the organization.

People Engagement, Performance Management & Team Development

• Build high-performing, engaged leadership teams through strong partnerships and data-informed people strategies.
• Use insights from surveys, exit interviews, and engagement data to improve employee experience and retain key talent.
• Facilitate the definition of SMART objectives aligned with business goals and support development across functions and geographies.

Organizational Development

• Facilitate structured organizational reviews to identify future capability needs and assess performance and potential.
• Lead change management efforts and support restructuring initiatives to ensure alignment and consistency across departments.
• Drive organizational agility and effectiveness.

Annual People Processes

• Facilitate and execute annual people processes in collaboration with business leaders.
• Ensure consistency and alignment across the business.

Strategic HR Initiatives

• Lead and contribute to cross-functional HR initiatives in partnership with HR Centers of Excellence.
• Align HR efforts with enterprise goals and future capability needs.
• Support senior-level recruitment as needed.

What You Bring

• 8+ years of HR experience with proven success partnering with senior leaders in complex, multinational environments.
• Strong business acumen and a results-oriented mindset, with expertise across organizational design, change management, performance, development, and data-driven decision-making.
• Collaborative and relationship-driven, with cultural agility and the ability to influence across borders and functions.
• Excellent project management skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders effectively.

jobs.title: HR Business Partner
jobs.description:
The Impact You'll Make

Danfoss is proud to be at the forefront of driving a global transformation in digital and electric solutions that increase productivity and energy efficiency. We are truly passionate about investment and innovation as we continue to support our customers' journey towards a greener and lower-carbon future. Our Editron business unit is leading the electrification revolution, specializing in hybrid and electric powertrain systems for the off-highway, on-highway and marine markets.

Following an internal move, we now have an opportunity for an HR Business Partner to join the Editron organisation, to be the primary HR partner for leaders within Editron, ensuring alignment between people initiatives and business priorities. As a member of the divisional leadership team, you will report to a member of the Human Resources Leadership Team and will lead a small team.

In this role you will be at the heart of our global transformation, shaping a more productive and energy-efficient future. As a trusted advisor and coach to senior leaders, you will spearhead strategic people initiatives that align with our business goals. You will play a crucial role in identifying and nurturing the skills and capabilities our workforce needs to meet future challenges. Your impact will be felt across the organization as you help us build a more effective, engaged, and future-ready team.

What You’ll Be Doing
• Acting as a strategic partner to business leaders, aligning HR initiatives with the core objectives of the Editron division.
• Leading organizational development and effectiveness by designing and implementing impactful HR strategies.
• Guiding our talent management and development programs to ensure we attract, develop, and retain the people who will drive our success.
• Serving as a change agent, guiding teams through transformation and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and innovation.
• Championing diversity, equity, and inclusion to create an environment where everyone feels they belong and can thrive.

What We're Looking For
• A background in Human Resources or a related field, with demonstrable experience as an HR Business Partner, preferably in a global and industrial setting.
• A strategic and forward-thinking mindset, combined with a hands-on and solution-oriented approach to getting things done.
• Experience in guiding organizational development, transformation, and leading teams through periods of change.
• Excellent communication and coaching skills, with a natural ability to build trust and rapport with people from all backgrounds and cultures.
• A collaborative spirit and the confidence to engage in constructive dialogue, challenge the status quo, and drive alignment across teams.

What You'll Get From Us
• We promote from within and support your learning with mentoring, training, and access to global opportunities.
• You’ll have flexibility, autonomy, and support to do your best work while maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Your well-being matters to us.

• You’ll receive benefits like annual bonus, paid vacation, pension plans, personal insurance, and more. These vary by country and contract, but they’re worth asking about—we think they’re pretty great.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you! Apply now to start the conversation and learn more about where your career can go with us.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected category.

jobs.title: Total Rewards Manager
jobs.description:
At myPOS, we’re all about helping businesses grow and get paid. We make payments simple, smart, and accessible for everyone, but we’re more than just payment solutions - myPOS is a partner in growth. From free multicurrency accounts to powerful e-commerce tools, we’re here to support business owners of all sizes and everyone out there who dreams of starting their own business.

As we are expanding our team, we’re looking for Total Rewards Manager to help us make a real difference in the Fintech industry. Ready to join us and shape the future of payments? Let’s make it happen!

About the role:

myPOS is scaling fast — a PE-backed fintech operating across 10 countries. Our people infrastructure needs to match our ambitions: the right reward framework, applied consistently, as the business evolves.

Our Radford job architecture is live and we're mid-way through rolling it out to the wider organisation. The EU Pay Transparency Directive is coming. Our compensation and benefits landscape is fragmented across geographies and needs someone who can bring consistency, rigour, and a clear point of view.

This is a hands-on specialist role. You'll own the day-to-day execution of compensation and benefits across the business — running cycles, managing data, advising on country-specific benefits, and ensuring our total reward framework is defensible, competitive, and consistently applied.

What You'll Do:

Compensation

• Own the operational running of our compensation cycles (mid-year and annual), working within the Radford job architecture and salary ranges already in place
• Maintain and update salary benchmarking data (Radford Global Technology Survey), ensuring ranges remain competitive at the 50th percentile against PE-backed fintech peers
• Support the rollout of our Compensation Philosophy to the wider organisation
• Advise on pay decisions for new hires, promotions, lateral moves and for acquisition companies — ensuring internal equity and market alignment
• Flag and resolve pay outliers; manage the remediation process with HRBPs
• Support EU Pay Transparency Directive readiness, including pay gap analysis and data documentation across all entities

MIP Administration

• Own the operational management of the Management Incentive Plan (MIP) in partnership with PE owners, Advent, including participant tracking, modelling, and documentation
• Maintain accurate MIP schedules — entry points, vesting, leaver provisions, and any changes resulting from org restructures or new hires
• Act as the day-to-day point of contact between HR and Advent on MIP-related queries; ensure data shared with them is accurate and timely
• Support any MIP communications to participants, ensuring clarity on how the plan works and what they're entitled to
• Flag any MIP implications arising from role changes, exits, or M&A activity before they become issues

Benefits

• Map and assess current benefits provision across all 10 countries (Bulgaria, UK, France, Italy, Ireland, Netherlands, Hungary, Germany, Austria, Belgium, Portugal) against local market norms and employee expectations
• Identify gaps, duplication, and inconsistencies; develop a benefits harmonisation roadmap that balances cost with competitiveness
• Manage relationships with benefits providers and brokers; lead renewals and any re-tendering
• Work with the HR Ops team to ensure benefits data flows correctly through BambooHR and Deel
• Act as the subject matter expert for country-specific statutory requirements — ensuring compliance across all jurisdictions

Data & Governance

• Maintain clean, accurate compensation and benefits data — you are the source of truth
• Produce regular reporting for HR leadership and, where relevant, the ELT
• Support any M&A activity with compensation and benefits due diligence

What We're Looking For:

• Minimum 8 years of experience in compensation and benefits, ideally in a multi-country tech or fintech environment
• Hands-on experience with Radford (or equivalent

jobs.description:
Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

Robinhood is on a mission to democratize finance for all — lowering barriers and expanding access so everyone can participate in the markets. Since our 2015 launch we've grown into one of the fastest-scaling brokerages ever, and that growth depends on hiring and keeping exceptional people. The Compensation team designs the programs that help Robinhood attract, motivate, and keep that talent as the company scales.

As a Senior Compensation Analyst, you'll own compensation analytics and the systems behind our broad-based base pay and variable comp programs. You'll build the models that drive pay decisions, run the tooling and workflows the People and Recruiting teams depend on, and use automation and AI to improve operations and enhance user experience. You'll operate across analysis, systems, and program execution — and have real ownership from day one.

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY; or Chicago, IL office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What You’ll Do

• Build and maintain compensation models. You'll develop scalable models that support market benchmarking, budget planning, scenario analysis, and data reconciliation, delivering data-driven insights that inform compensation strategy and business decisions.
• Lead compensation analytics. You'll drive survey participation, job matching, market pricing, and trend analyses to evaluate pay competitiveness and inform salary structures, equity bands, and compensation recommendations across global markets.
• Design and maintain reporting and trackers. You'll create and maintain compensation trackers, dashboards, and budgets, delivering accurate, timely reporting that stakeholders can rely on.
• Administer broad-based compensation. You'll support annual merit, promotion, and variable/incentive compensation cycles end to end, including planning, modeling, award generation, payroll/equity reconciliation, and post-cycle analysis.
• Build and improve compensation systems. You'll maintain and enhance the compensation tooling, job catalog, and databases used by the People and Recruiting teams, and design automations that reduce manual work and error.
• Support M&A integration. You'll provide compensation analysis and support for mergers and acquisitions, including due diligence, harmonizing pay structures, and integrating acquired employees into Robinhood's programs.
• Further AI and automation across the function. You'll use AI and modern tooling to enhance and streamline benchmarking, analysis, communications, and reporting, making processes faster and more accurate.
• Partner cross-functionally. You'll work with People Partners, HRIS, Finance, and Legal on year-round initiatives and ad-hoc analyses, ensuring clean data flows and clear communication.

What You Bring

• 4–6 years of compensation experience
• Advanced Excel/Google Sheets modeling with large datasets
• Hands-on experience with HRIS, Compensation Data

jobs.title: Manager, Compensation
jobs.description:
Ventra is a leading business solutions provider for facility-based physicians practicing anesthesia, emergency medicine, hospital medicine, pathology, and radiology. Focused on Revenue Cycle Management, Ventra partners with private practices, hospitals, health systems, and ambulatory surgery centers to deliver transparent and data-driven solutions that solve the most complex revenue and reimbursement issues, enabling clinicians to focus on providing outstanding care to their patients and communities.

Come Join Our Team!

• As part of our robust Rewards & Recognition program, this role is eligible for our Ventra performance-based incentive plan, because we believe great work deserves great rewards

Help Us Grow Our Dream Team — Join Us, Refer a Friend, and Earn a Referral Bonus!

Job Summary

• The Manager, Compensation is responsible for the day-to-day governance and administration of compensation programs for Ventra, ensuring pay decisions are consistent, competitive, and compliant with local regulations. This role manages offer and internal movement approvals, supports the annual salary review and bonus cycles, maintains job grading and salary structures, and partners closely with Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, Payroll and other HR stakeholders to ensure accurate and timely execution of compensation processes. This is a hands-on role suited for a compensation professional with solid technical grounding who is ready to own a full-cycle compensation portfolio for the India market.

Essential Functions And Tasks

• Review and approve compensation for new hire offers and internal movements (promotions, transfers, lateral moves), ensuring alignment with salary structures, internal equity, and budget guidelines.
• Administer the annual salary review cycle, including data preparation, modeling, guideline development, manager enablement, and post-cycle audits.
• Administer the annual bonus/incentive cycle, including calculation methodology , eligibility checks, payout modeling, and reconciliation with Finance and Payroll.
• Manage incentive plan administration for applicable colleagues , ensuring accuracy and timely payout in coordination with relevant stakeholders.
• Own job evaluation and grading for new and existing job descriptions, applying job evaluation methodology consistently across the organization.
• Maintain and periodically update salary structures/pay bands based on market benchmarking and internal equity analysis.
• Monitor and ensure compliance with applicable labor laws and statutory requirements relating to compensation (e.g., minimum wage rules, bonus act provisions, gratuity, PF, tax as relevant to comp design).
• Partner with the Payroll team to ensure accurate translation of compensation decisions into payroll processing, resolving discrepancies as needed.
• Support internal audits and statutory/regulatory reporting requirements related to compensation.
• Prepare compensation analyses, reports, and dashboards for HR and business leadership as needed.
• Respond to compensation-related queries from HRBPs, managers, and employees, providing guidance grounded in policy and market data.
• Support ad hoc compensation projects (e.g., market benchmarking studies, pay equity analysis, new market entry pay structures) as assigned.

Education And Experience Requirements

• Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Psychology, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field required;
• 5–6 years of progressive experience in compensation management or total rewards, ideally within a multinational, shared services, or matrixed organization.
• Demonstrated experience managing salary review and bonus cycles end-to-end.
• Experience with job evaluation/grading methodologies (e.g., Mercer IPE, Korn Ferry/Hay, Willis Towers Watson, or similar).
• Working knowledge of statutory compliance requirements for India / US / Philippines as they relate to compensation.
• Experience in using HRIS and/or compensation planning tool

This role sits within our Total Rewards team and puts you at the center of executive compensation and equity strategy, shaping long-term incentive design, advising leadership on pay decisions, and making sure our approach is competitive, fair, and unmistakably Supercell.

You'll work at both a strategic and hands-on level. Think: designing executive equity programs one day, and modeling grant scenarios the next. You'll partner closely with our Total Rewards Lead, Compensation Manager, Finance, and senior leadership to evolve how we think about executive pay globally.

What You'll Be Doing

• Own and continuously improve Supercell's executive compensation programs, base salary, annual incentives, and long-term incentive structures.

• Design and manage and equity frameworks that stay aligned with company performance, strategy, and market competitiveness.
• Co-own global incentive programs (short- and long-term) with the Compensation Manager, ensuring consistency across employee and executive populations.
• Act as the go-to expert on executive compensation and equity, advising senior leadership on pay decisions, offers, retention strategies, and long-term incentive design.
• Develop and maintain compensation and equity guidelines, governance, and decision frameworks that ensure consistency, fairness, and alignment with how we operate.
• Keep our executive comp and equity practices competitive through market benchmarking and external insights.
• Ensure compliance with relevant regulations, governance standards, and internal policies across all markets.

• Partner with Finance on compensation and equity cost modeling, forecasting, and long-term incentive planning.
• Support reporting needs related to executive comp and equity, including internal governance and external disclosures where applicable.
• Partner with senior leadership to provide clear, data-driven guidance on executive compensation and equity decisions.
• Act as a trusted advisor on complex, sensitive, or high-impact compensation and equity topics.
• From time to time, provide hands-on support for Americas-based compensation activities, such as offer benchmarking or benefits queries, when additional coverage is needed.

What You Have

• 10+ years of experience in compensation, with deep experience in executive compensation and equity design and management.
• Strong understanding of executive compensation structures, including short- and long-term incentives (bonuses, RSUs, equity plans).
• Solid analytical skills and hands-on experience with financial modeling, equity scenarios, and long-term incentive planning.
• Experience advising senior stakeholders and navigating sensitive or complex compensation conversations.
• Good understanding of market practices, governance, and regulatory considerations related to executive comp and equity.
• Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills, you're comfortable building models and analysis from scratch.
• Experience working with HRIS and compensation planning tools.
• A proactive, ownership-driven mindset, you set priorities and drive work forward independently.
• Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills.
• Clear communication and presentation skills in English.
• You're actively using AI tools in your day-to-day work, and excited about experimenting with new ways AI can improve how we work.

jobs.title: Total Rewards Specialist
jobs.description:
WE ARE HIRING

As an AVASO employee, you will be part of a global organization that provides IT Services to big national and international clients across multiple industries. We are an IT solution provider with coverage in more than 170 countries as well as global distribution capabilities. We have a proven track record of success in providing best-of-breed technology solutions to enterprises of all sizes, including some of the world’s largest brands. AVASO offers you an excellent growth opportunity with a strong global company and good money.

Website: - https://www.avasotech.com/

Position : Total Rewards Specialist
Experience : 3 - 6 years
Position Type : Full-Time
Location : Mohali

Job Overview
Currently seeking an energetic and results-oriented Total Rewards Specialist to join our fast-paced, full life cycle recruitment team; supporting field support and proposal recruitment. This position is responsible for thorough execution of AVASO’s recruiting process for assigned searches, and requires an eye for detail, a passion for finding top talent, and an ability to multi-task in a fast-paced environment. This is a full-time role and requires the ability to plan, multi-task and follow through on assigned tasks.

What You'll Do
Compensation Administration
• Support the annual merit cycle — preparing employee-level CTC data, working on the data and analysis.
• Assist in salary benchmarking exercises using approved survey sources; maintain salary range tables, grade band schedules, and CTC revision trackers.
• Process salary revisions, promotions, and increments accurately in the HRIS and payroll system.
• Prepare compensation analyses, identify outliers, and flag findings for review by the Senior Specialist or Manager.

Payroll Operations Support
• Coordinate monthly payroll inputs: LOP deductions, arrear computations, ad-hoc allowances, and one-time payments.
• Validate payroll data for accuracy prior to processing; cross-check outputs against HRIS records and resolve discrepancies.
• Maintain structured payroll trackers, salary revision logs, and exception registers in Excel.
• Liaise with the Finance team for payroll reconciliation and monthly variance reporting.

Exit Management & Full and Final Settlement (FNF)
• Own end-to-end FNF computation for exiting employees.
• Coordinate with HR Operations, Finance, and business units to obtain clearances and validate inputs before FNF is processed.
• Serve as the primary point of contact for employee and ex-employee queries on FNF, salary arrears, tax deductions, and relieving documentation.
• Maintain a live FNF tracker covering all active cases, status, pending clearances, and disbursement dates.

HR Data Analysis & Reporting — A Core Part of This Role
• We are looking for someone who treats data as a first-class output. The ability to build, automate analytics clearly is as important as the operational skills in this role.
• Build and maintain Excel-based dashboards and trackers for headcount cost, payroll variance, and compensation distribution.
• Develop VBA macros to automate repetitive payroll and HR processes, reducing manual effort and improving accuracy.
• Analyse data to identify trends, outliers, and equity issues.
• Proactively flag and resolve data quality issues across all Total Rewards records.

What We're Looking For
Experience
• 5–6 years of progressive experience in Total Rewards, Compensation & Benefits, or HR Operations.
• Demonstrated hands-on experience in payroll processing, salary revision administration, and FNF management.
• Prior experience in a mid-to-large IT services, technology, or global services organisation is preferred.
• Exposure to multi-country compensation structures is an advantage.

Data & Analytics Skills — Required
• Strong Excel proficiency is a hard requirement for this role — not just data entry or basic formulas.
• Microsoft Excel (Advanced) — VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, INDEX-MATCH, SUMIFS, Pivot Tables, dynamic dashboards, data validation.

jobs.description:
We take play seriously. We’re looking for curious adventurers ready to find their party, fueled by imagination and drive to build what’s never been built before. At Hasbro and Wizards of the Coast, you’ll collaborate with passionate teams to reimagine our iconic brands and create experiences that spark joy, connection, and community through the magic of play. This is your chance to shape legendary play that lasts a lifetime.

Job Description

The Compensation team leads compensation programs for Hasbro. Our work impacts every employee globally through the programs we coordinate. The team also has a meaningful role to play by ensuring our employee value proposition is competitive in the marketplace and financially balanced.

We are looking for a Compensation Consultant to lead this effort across EMEA and APAC. The incumbent shall partner closely with local HR teams and leaders to build and implement compensation programs. This role will provide direction and strategic solutions for compensation matters considering both business and HR priorities, market practices, and emerging trends.

A Day In The Life Of a Compensation Consultant

• Lead compensation programs including but not limited to; market benchmarking reviews, compensation planning, recognition programs, offer development, retention programs, and budget management.
• Play a meaningful role in advising and educating key business stakeholders, HR Business Partners and Talent Acquisition on our compensation philosophy, to include the following components: base, variable, sales and equity compensation, as well as cyclical and ad-hoc compensation programs.
• Partner and collaborate closely with vital team members and client groups to understand organizational needs and prioritize accordingly. Providing compensation insights to support strategic decisions.
• Proactively assess internal and external trends, relevant pay legislation, market intelligence, and potential impact to our pay philosophy including our pay transparency projects.
• Provide consultation, mentoring and sophisticated advice to HR Business Partners and business leaders.
• Partner with Finance teams to craft and develop incentive plans and support formal plan governance and oversight activities.
• Represent the voice of the customer in the design of enterprise-wide pay programs and lead the design for client pay program.
• Operate with a high degree of autonomy in managing compensation programs and analyses, applying sound judgment while ensuring alignment with company guidelines and governance standards.

What You'll Bring

• Bachelor's or equivalent; proven track record in compensation.
• Experience crafting, developing and owning a variety of compensation programs and processes including base salary, variable pay programs, sales compensation, compensation strategy and competitive pay analysis.
• Deep analytical skills with an ability to break down sophisticated questions / data into well-structured analyses and synthesize key points.
• Forward-thinking with ability to think end-to-end.
• Ability to influence and communicate with executive audiences.
• Skilled in building consultative partnerships.
• Proven experience in advising across regions, ideally with experience supporting not only EMEA but also APAC.
• Solid experience in working in matrix global organization, flexible in management style across various cultures and backgrounds.

Employees may be eligible for annual and long-term incentives as part of their overall compensation package, depending on role, location, and eligibility. Benefits and programs may include:

• Health & Wellness
• Time Off to Recharge
• Financial Well-being
• Life & Family Support
• Volunteer and Community Initiatives
• Learning & Development
• Exclusive Perks

For everyone, everywhere.

jobs.title: Senior Rewards Manager
jobs.description:
Brief Info About Vinted

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third.

The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people.

Information About The Position

Our People team play a key role in building this - they are the architects of our organisation and the custodians of our culture.

As a Senior Rewards Manager at Vinted, you will play a critical role in designing, implementing, and evolving our total rewards strategy to support employee motivation, performance, and retention across all markets. Working closely with People Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, and Finance, you will ensure our compensation and benefits frameworks are competitive, equitable, and aligned with Vinted’s culture and growth ambitions. This role combines hands-on project ownership with strategic partnership and data-driven analysis.

In this position, you’ll

• Design and maintain compensation structures (e.g. salary bands, job levelling frameworks) in partnership with key People and Finance stakeholders.

• Drive rewards-related projects such as new country launches, M&A integrations, or total rewards policy refreshes

• Experience with Workday and compensation survey tools (e.g. Radford, Mercer) is a plus.

jobs.title: Compensation Analyst
jobs.description:
Xometry (NASDAQ: XMTR) powers the industries of today and tomorrow by connecting the people with big ideas to the manufacturers who can bring them to life. Xometry’s digital marketplace gives manufacturers the critical resources they need to grow their business while also making it easy for buyers at Fortune 1000 companies to tap into global manufacturing capacity.

We are seeking a data-driven and detail-oriented Compensation Analyst to join our Total Rewards team in Bengaluru. In this role, you will be instrumental in ensuring our pay practices remain competitive, equitable, and aligned with our global growth strategy. You will serve as a subject matter expert on market trends, job architecture, and the execution of our annual rewards cycle.

Key Responsibilities

• Market Intelligence: Lead the end-to-end participation in global salary surveys (e.g., Aon Radford, Mercer, WTW). This includes data mapping, submission, and analyzing results to identify market movement.
• Salary Range Development: Design and maintain competitive salary structures and pay grades. You will use market data to build and refresh ranges that support our hiring and retention goals.
• Job Architecture: Support the maintenance of our global job catalog. You will evaluate new and existing roles, ensuring they are leveled correctly within our internal framework.
• Annual Cycle Management: Act as a core contributor to the year-end Base Salary, Bonus, and Equity planning process. This includes preparing manager workbooks, auditing recommendations, and ensuring budget compliance.
• Data Analytics: Create and maintain complex compensation models. You will provide "what-if" cost analyses for leadership to support headcount planning and pay-for-performance initiatives.
• Collaboration: Partner with HR Business Partners and Talent Acquisition on compensation-related matters, including offer and promotion recommendations.

Required Skills & Qualifications

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Finance, Mathematics, or a related field.
• Experience: 3–5years of dedicated experience in Compensation or People Analytics, preferably within a fast-paced technology sector or global shared-services environment. Knowledge of compensation principles, market pricing, and salary structures.
• Technical Savvy: Expert-level proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets. You must be comfortable managing large datasets using advanced formulas, Pivot Tables, and XLOOKUPs.
• HRIS Systems: Proficiency with HRIS platforms such as ADP, Workday, Dayforce, or UKG. Experience with ADP is specifically advantageous as we navigate our current infrastructure.
• Analytical Mindset: Ability to translate raw data into actionable insights and present findings clearly to stakeholders.

High Integrity: Proven ability to maintain strict confidentiality and accuracy when handling sensitive employee payroll and equity data.

#Promoted

Xometry is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status.

For US based roles: Xometry participates in E-Verify and after a job offer is accepted, will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.

Job Description

Human Resources Business Partner, EMEA

Position Summary

The Human Resources Business Partner (HRBP), EMEA supports leaders and employees across the Europe, Middle East and Africa region by providing guidance on employee relations, organizational effectiveness, workforce planning, performance management, employee development, and talent acquisition.

As the primary HR contact for assigned client groups, the HRBP works closely with managers to support business objectives, strengthen team effectiveness, address employee matters, and help build a positive and productive work environment. The role also partners with leaders to attract, retain, and develop talent while ensuring compliance with local employment legislation and company policies.

Key Responsibilities

Business Partnership

• Partner with managers to understand business priorities, workforce challenges, and organizational needs.
• Provide guidance on workforce planning, team effectiveness, organizational structure, and employee-related matters.
• Support leaders in identifying talent needs, succession considerations, and development opportunities.
• Assist managers in addressing business and people challenges while balancing operational and employee needs.

Employee Relations

• Advise managers and employees on workplace concerns, performance matters, policy interpretation, and employment-related issues.
• Ensure consistent and fair application of company policies and practices.
• Support conflict resolution and employee relations initiatives.

Knowledge & Skills

• Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
• Excellent communication and influencing abilities

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

• Extreme ownership. Full autonomy. Own things end to end often taking on scope outside your core role without being asked to get things done.
• Velocity. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.
• First principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.
• Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

About The Role

We're seeking an exceptional Compensation Manager who is equal parts strategist and practitioner. You won't just administer comp cycles — you'll operate as a trusted partner to the business, using rigorous market research and data to shape compensation philosophy, drive incentive design, and build the tools and frameworks that support talent decisions across the company.

This role demands both scientific precision and practical judgment. The real value you bring is your ability to move fluidly between market analysis and execution — turning complex data into clear recommendations, building compensation infrastructure that cross-functional teams can actually use, and supporting critical moments like performance cycles and offer decisions with speed and confidence. Fluidstack is building the backbone of AI — your work ensures the people doing that building are recognized and retained accordingly.

• Drive compensation planning: Own annual and off-cycle comp planning processes end-to-end, ensuring alignment between business strategy, talent priorities, and budget — and stay hands-on through execution.
• Build tools that serve the business: Design and maintain compensation tools, models, and resources that support cross-functional needs — from offer decisioning and leveling guidance to performance cycle support — making it easier for People, Finance, and leadership to act with confidence.

Grab is Southeast Asia's leading superapp. From getting your favourite meals delivered to helping you manage your finances and getting around town hassle-free, we've got your back with everything. The Rewards team, which sits within People Operations (Pops) team, drives all global compensation and benefits programmes in Grab. You will guide rewards programmes based on an analytical approach balanced with judgement.

About Us

The Public Service Commission (PSC) is government’s human resources organization supporting departments, agencies, and employees to deliver programs and services to Nova Scotians. We are committed to building a collaborative and inclusive public service grounded in respect, integrity, diversity, accountability, and the public good.

The PSC establishes human resource policies, programs, standards, and procedures, and provides direction, advice, and support to departments to ensure consistent, effective application across government.

We are focused on the current and future needs of the provincial workforce to ensure the public service is equipped to meet the demands of a growing and changing province.

About Our Opportunity

Reporting to the Managing Director of Compensation, or Compensation Lead, the Corporate Compensation Consultant provides expert compensation advice and develops practical, evidence-based compensation solutions for the Province of Nova Scotia. Flo is the world’s #1 health & fitness app worldwide on a mission to build a better future for female health. Backed by a $200M investment led by General Atlantic, we became the first product of our kind to reach a $1B valuation in 2024 – and we’re not slowing down.

The job
Flo's growth has been rapid and intentional. From a few hundred employees to a global team of 500+, we've scaled by building high-performing, empowered teams. As we continue to evolve, we're hiring a strategic, commercially sharp, and hands-on HR Business Partner to partner across our business functions.
You will work directly with senior leadership, helping shape capability, structure, and performance so that teams can move faster, prioritise smarter, and scale sustainably.
This role is not about policy administration, it's about driving organisational performance.
How we think about HRBP at Flo
Our HRBPs are business partners first, functional specialists second.
We operate as a tight, high-performing team and consider ourselves interchangeable and function-agnostic. You will be embedded in a function, but your remit is to solve business problems, not to stay confined to one area.

• Deeply understanding business strategy, not just People processes

• Thinking enterprise-wide, not in silos

We expect our HRBPs to operate at company level, even when embedded in a function.

jobs.title: Lead People Partner
jobs.description:
We’re a global team of over 400 people, working together to push the boundaries of open-source technology and multi-cloud solutions. Our vision is to help developers, builders, and creators bring their ideas to life with speed and simplicity, by providing a cloud data platform that makes open-source databases, search, streaming, and application infrastructure easily accessible to everyone.

The Role

As Lead People Partner, you will collaborate with the CPTO and their leadership team to build talent-dense organisations, plan ahead for the talent they need, and make sure Aiven's people strategy actually shows up in how the function runs.

You're not just implementing what the People team designs. You help shape what it is, then make it land in your function in a way that works. You're also a senior voice on what the People function builds and prioritises across the company.

Leaders treat you as a peer who challenges and supports them, not as someone who runs HR processes on their behalf.

What You'll Do

• Exec advisory: Act as a strategic advisor to your C-suite and VP-level leaders. Shape how they build their organisations, manage and develop their top talent, and retain the people they can't afford to lose.
• People strategy for your functions: Co-create the people strategy for your functions with functional leadership. Understand the business well enough to know what's needed, and push back when the ask isn't the right answer.
• Talent density: Set the standard for how talent density is built and maintained in your functions, through 9-box, career frameworks, stay interviews, and succession planning. Keep an honest, current view of where the organisation is strong, where it's thin, and what needs to change.
• Manager accountability: Drive the shift to managers owning their people outcomes instead of leaning on HR, ensuring managers have the skills, tools, and expectation to handle it themselves.
• Total rewards, levelling, and DEI: Own total rewards alignment and levelling consistency across your functions. Champion diversity at senior leadership level, in how promotions, succession, and hiring decisions get made.
• Workforce planning: Think 6–12 months ahead with your functional leaders on headcount, capability, and team shape. Lead the headcount planning squads with the functional Guilds (TA and FP&A).
• AI-first behaviours: Sponsor AI-native career frameworks in your functions, and drive AI-first behaviours in how your functional leaders and their teams work.
• Collaborate with wider People team: When a people product needs to be built, company-wide or specific to your function, you’ll influence and collaborate with the wider people team, bring the functional insight, frame the problem, and stay involved as the work develops.
• Raising the team: Mentor and coach P3 and P4 PBPs, and help the whole team produce better work, not just your own patch.
• Company-wide influence: Be a key voice in what the People function prioritises and builds across the business, bringing the perspective of the functions you support.

What We're Looking For

• Proven experience as a senior HR/People Business Partner operating at executive level, ideally supporting C-suite and VP-level leaders directly.
• A track record of building high-density organisations: succession planning, career frameworks, and performance calibration that actually change outcomes, not just complete a process.
• The range to zoom out to org design and succession planning, then zoom back into a hard performance conversation in the same day.
• A clear, confident point of view on how strong organisations get built, backed by the confidence to challenge senior leaders rather than facilitate their process for them.
• A history of raising the quality of the people around you, not just your own work.

Amazing! What's Next

If you think Aiven is the place for you and our values align with yours, send us your resume and we'll get in touch.

Unframe is an AI-first startup helping the world’s largest enterprises bring LLM-powered applications to life in days - not months. We combine the speed of a product company with the flexibility of a consultancy, helping customers move from idea to deployed AI systems faster than anyone else in the market.

About The Role

As our first dedicated People Partner in Israel, you’ll own the entire employee lifecycle and play a key role in shaping how we support, develop, and scale our people. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys building strong people practices while partnering closely with managers to create high-performing teams.

You’ll be the go-to partner for managers across the organization, helping them navigate performance, employee relations, leadership development, and organizational challenges. You’ll also own the operational side of the employee experience, ensuring every stage of the employee lifecycle is consistent, thoughtful, and aligned with our culture.

What You’ll Do

• Own the end-to-end employee lifecycle for our Israel team, from onboarding through offboarding.
• Work in close partnership with the recruiting team in Israel to accelerate hiring, streamline recruitment processes, and proactively remove obstacles throughout the hiring lifecycle.
• Partner closely with managers on performance management, employee development, promotions, compensation cycles, and day-to-day people decisions.
• Coach managers on leadership best practices, feedback conversations, performance improvement, difficult conversations, and employee relations.
• Design and deliver manager enablement programs and leadership training for both new and experienced managers.
• Lead annual and ongoing performance review processes, ensuring consistency and high-quality execution across the organization.
• Drive employee engagement initiatives and continuously improve the employee experience and build the culture within the office
• Support organizational changes, team effectiveness, and people-related decision making.
• Identify trends and organizational challenges using people data and recommend practical solutions.
• Partner with the global People team to ensure alignment where relevant while tailoring processes for the Israeli organization.

What We’re Looking For

• 6–8+ years of experience in HR, People Partner, or HRBP roles within fast-growing technology startups.
• A hands-on mindset with the ability to move seamlessly between strategic thinking and operational execution.
• Demonstrated experience leading and developing a talent acquisition team.
• Previous experience supporting managers and leadership teams in a high-growth environment.
• Proven experience leading performance management, employee relations, and organizational processes.
• Experience coaching managers through complex people situations with confidence and sound judgment.
• Strong knowledge of Israeli employment law and HR best practices.

You’ll partner closely with leaders across the company, drive meaningful initiatives, and make a direct impact on our culture, employee experience, and continued growth.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant, Human Resources
jobs.description:
Medison offers hope to patients suffering from rare and severe diseases, by forming partnerships with emerging biotech companies to accelerate access to highly innovative therapies in international markets.

As the creator and leader of the global partnership category in the pharma industry, we strive to be Always Ahead, and work relentlessly to bring therapy to patients in need, no matter where they live.

Our values are at the core of every action we take, and we are committed to going above and beyond for the benefit of the patients we serve.

We are a dynamic, fast-paced company, operating in over 30 countries on 5 continents. We are looking for out-of-the-box thinkers, people who are passionate, caring, agile and adaptive, to join us on our mission. If you are looking to make a difference in people's lives, we invite you to join us!

The Executive Assistant will provide administrative and operational support to the HR team and personal assistance to the Chief People Officer (CPO).

Responsibilities:

• Manage sensitive matters with a high level of confidentiality and discretion
• Sustain a daily calendar of meetings and events, including scheduling onsite and virtual meetings with multiple internal & external participants and booking conference rooms
• Arrange travels and accommodations for the CPO and team members
• Support HR budget management and control, including purchase orders and expense reports (invoices and POs)
• Coordinate and prepare internal reports and presentations within the department and to management
• Lead and coordinate various projects within and outside the department
• Arrange and coordinate all HR departments social activities and events (offsite meetings, holiday toasts, birthdays, volunteering, etc.)
• Work closely with the Employee Experience manager in arranging site events for all employees in Israel
• Working closely with the Talent Management, Learning and Development in arranging workshops and learning activities

Requirements:

• At least 3 years of experience in office administration of senior management
• Excellent level of English (reading, writing, and speaking)
• Proficient in Microsoft Office - Outlook, Word, PPT
• High attention to details and problem-solving orientation
• Resourceful, fast learner, and knows how to manage unexpected situations
• Service orientation and "can do" attitude with a high standard of ethics
• Strong ability to multitask, prioritize, and thrive in a fast-paced environment
• Outstanding organizational skills
• Excellent ability to work with multiple interfaces

jobs.title: HR Business Partner (Maternity Leave Replacement)
jobs.description:
You’ll serve as a strategic advisor to managers and leaders, aligning people strategies with business objectives. You’ll act as a trusted consultant, helping leaders build high-performing teams, make data-driven people decisions, and foster a culture that supports Alice's mission and goals.

This is a hybrid position; you’ll be asked to be in our office in Ramat Gan three times per week.

Key Responsibilities

• Partner with managers and leaders to align people strategies with business objectives and organizational priorities.
• Use people analytics and workforce data to identify trends, inform decisions, and address organizational risks and opportunities.
• Drive talent management initiatives, including workforce planning, succession planning, retention, and leadership development.
• Partner with Talent Acquisition and hiring managers to support hiring plans, organizational growth, and critical talent needs.
• Coach managers on performance management, employee relations, leadership effectiveness, and team development.
• Support employee engagement, culture, and organizational effectiveness initiatives, including survey analysis and action planning.
• Partner with leaders to manage organizational change, restructures, and transformation initiatives.
• Advise on compensation, promotions, policy interpretation, compliance, and other people-related matters to ensure consistent and effective people practices.

Requirements:

Required

• 5-7 years of experience as an HRBP in a global organization.
• Strong knowledge of employment law and HR best practices in Israel.
• Experience in a matrixed technology organization.
• Strong preference for experience partnering with R&D teams with fast-paced work and short turnaround requirements for meeting customer’s goals.
• Proven experience in identifying and leading change, and building this capability in others.
• Proven ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution, driving impactful outcomes in fast-paced environments.
• Strong track record of coaching and partnering with senior leaders and frontline managers to elevate leadership effectiveness and organizational performance.
• Highly analytical and data-driven mindset, with the ability to turn insights into clear, actionable HR strategies aligned with business needs.
• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with high emotional intelligence and the ability to influence across all levels while balancing empathy and accountability.
• Fluent Hebrew and English.

About Alice:

Alice is a trust, safety, and security company built for the AI era. We safeguard the communicative technologies people use to create, collaborate, and interact—whether with each other or with machines.

In a world where AI has fundamentally changed the nature of risk, Alice provides end-to-end coverage across the entire AI lifecycle. We support frontier model labs, enterprises, and UGC platforms with a comprehensive suite of solutions: from model hardening evaluations and pre-deployment red-teaming to runtime guardrails and ongoing drift detection.

jobs.title: HR Business Partner
jobs.description:
We are Bobcat. A community powered by people. Across 16 countries and 50 nationalities, we have over 2,500 employees, 300 dealers in EMEA and a world-class innovation centre that’s breaking new ground every day. We’ve been engineering powerful machines and transforming how the world works for more than 60 years. From construction to agriculture, our products make an impact. We empower people to accomplish more, and we’re proud of that. It’s our people that make it possible. We value the skill and expertise that surrounds us. As part of our team, you’ll find career opportunities that will challenge, inspire, and reward you. We believe that together we can unearth something extraordinary.

We are looking for HR Business Partner to join our team at Bobcat.

As HR Business Partner at Bobcat, you’ll play a key role in our community. You will partner with leaders and employees across EMEA to shape our organisation, support the full employee life cycle, and drive people initiatives that enable business growth and transformation.

We're Looking For Someone Who

• Partners with leaders on workforce planning and organisational design.
• Supports organisational changes and reviews job descriptions.
• Drives talent management activities, including succession planning, performance management, and leadership development.
• Partners with Learning & Development on training, career mobility, and development.
• Collaborates on compensation processes, including salary reviews, merit, and job evaluation.
• Manages employee relations matters, including disciplinary cases, grievances, redundancies, internal transfers, onboarding, and exit interviews.
• Supports employee engagement initiatives and helps strengthen the Employee Value Proposition.
• Analyses HR metrics and provides insights to support business decisions.
• Supports recruitment activities and future hiring needs.

What Sets You Apart

• Around 10 years of HR business partnering experience in an international environment.
• Experience in HR administration and at least one HR CoE area, such as C&B, Talent Management, or Talent Acquisition.
• Strong knowledge of employment law across multiple EMEA countries, with hands-on labour law experience in at least one country.
• Experience with organisational design and change management.
• Good business acumen and understanding of how business priorities shape people strategies.
• Strong analytical skills and experience working with KPIs and HR data.
• Fluent in English and ideally another EMEA language.
• Proficiency in MS Office, especially Excel and PowerPoint.

What You Get In Return

• Motivating salary and benefits – a contribution to pension insurance of 3% of gross salary, meal vouchers, etc.
• Hybrid work – enjoy working from home for two days a week.
• Dynamic and innovative working environment – modern offices with fully equipped facilities.
• Opportunity to become part of a global market leader.
• Room for further personal and professional growth – career development, training, and education.

At Bobcat, we support equal opportunities, value diversity of skills, perspectives and cultures and encourage applications from candidates from all backgrounds.

jobs.title: מנהל.ת יחידת שכר, תגמול והטבות באגף משאבי אנוש בהנהלה
jobs.description:
קצת על התפקיד

הסמכות הניהולית הבכירה באגף משאבי אנוש שבאחריותה הגדרה והטמעה של אסטרטגיית ומדיניות שכר, תגמול והטבות.
כפיפות: סמנכ"לית בכירה למשאבי אנוש

במסגרת התפקיד:
• מומחיות ידע ותוכן בנושאי שכר, תגמול והטבות.
• ניהול תקציב השכר כמרכז מומחיות לבקרה תקציבית וניהולי כולל בחינה דיפרנציאלית של חלוקת התקציב.
• הגדרה והטמעה של מדיניות השכר, תגמול וההטבות על פי החלטות הנהלה והסכמים ותוך עמידה בדרישות החוק ובצרכים העסקיים והתחרותיים של הארגון.
• הגדרת תוכניות, תהליכים וכלים תומכים בכל רכיבי התגמול, כולל:
• שכר - טווחי שכר לתפקידים, מדיניות שכר לגיוס ושינוי מעמד (שינוי תפקיד, הסבות וכו'), מדיניות מתן תוספות שכר.
• תגמול משתנה כגון בונוסים ומענקי הצטיינות.
• הטבות כגון פנסיה, קרן השתלמות, אחזקת רכב, ארוחות, ליסינג, פלאפון, הלוואות וכו'.
• אחריות על מדיניות וניהול ההסכמים מול מנהלי ההסדרים וספקים כגון פנסיה, ביטוחי מנהלים, קרנות השתלמות.
• אחריות על תמיכה שוטפת בנושאי תגמול והטבות כולל הקניית ידע והנגשת תוכן המדיניות - העברת הדרכות בנושאי שכר, תגמול והטבות לעובדים ולמנהלים ותמיכה באוכלוסיית ה- HRBPs ומנהלות התגמול החטיבתיות.
• הגדרה ועדכון של טווחי השכר, ביצוע תקופתי של סקרי שכר ועדכון טווחי השכר בארגון מול הגדרות צבירן וניהול הקשר מול צבירן.
• ניתוחים שונים והכנת מודלים ותחזיות בתחום שכר ועלויות שכר. בנייה והגדרת כלי סימולציה כלכליים לצורך גיבוש החלטות במסגרת הליכי מו"מ.
• מתן מידע תומך החלטות בתחום התגמול, הגדרה והפקה של דוחות בתחום השכר ועלויות שכר להנהלה, לחטיבות וכן אחריות על הוצאת מידע ודיווח בנושא שכר לכלל בעלי עניין הפנימיים והחיצוניים.
• אחריות על הגדרת שכר והטבות וליווי לעובדים ביציאה ל- Re-location ונציגויות רפאל בעולם.
• אחריות על הטמעת מדיניות חוזי עבודה בכירים וליווי שוטף בנושאים אלו.
• אחריות ליישום הסכמים קיבוציים בהיבטי שכר והטבות.
• ניהול ועמידה בביקורות חיצוניות ופנימיות: SOX, משרד האוצר, רשות החברות כולל דיווחים שוטפים לרשויות.
• הנחייה מקצועית של מנהלי התגמול החטיבתיים.
• משימות נוספות שיוגדרו מעת לעת.

מה אנחנו מחפשים?

• תואר ראשון בכלכלה / סטטיסטיקה / חשבונאות / הנדסת תעשיה וניהול / מנהל עסקים, או תואר דומה אחר.
• תואר שני - יתרון.
• ניסיון של 5 שנים לפחות בתחומי השכר וההטבות, כולל ניסיון מוכח בבניית תוכניות תגמול מורכבות.
• ניסיון בעבודה עם הסכמים קיבוציים – יתרון.
• שליטה מלאה בתוכנות אופיס בדגש על אקסל (רמה מתקדמת), כולל ניסיון בעבודה עם כלי BI.
• שליטה בשיטות סטטיסטיות וטכניקות מודלים פיננסיים.
• יכולת מוכחת של ניהול ממשקים מול גורמי פנים וחוץ כגון גופי ממשלה, ספקים ויועצים.
• יכולת מוכחת של ניהול תהליכים מורכבים בסביבה רוויית ממשקים וניהול צוותי עבודה.
• כישורים:
• יכולת אנליטית גבוהה, יכולת ניתוח נתונים.
• יכולת עבודה והצגה מול קהלים מגוונים לרבות דרגים בכירים.
• יכולת ביטוי גבוהה בכתב ובע"פ, כולל הכנת מצגות, תרגום נתונים ודוחות מפורטים.
• יחסי אנוש מעולים ותקשורת בין אישית ברמה גבוהה.

jobs.title: Total Rewards Specialist
jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced Total Rewards Specialist to join our team at Power International Holding. This role is responsible for supporting the design, implementation, and continuous enhancement of the organization's Total Rewards strategy, ensuring competitive compensation, benefits, and recognition programs that attract, retain, and motivate top talent.
If you have a strong background in compensation and benefits, job evaluation, salary benchmarking, HR analytics, and Total Rewards within a large corporate environment, we'd love to hear from you.

Key Responsibilities
• Support the development and execution of Total Rewards strategies, policies, and programs.
• Conduct job evaluations using recognized methodologies and internal benchmarking.
• Perform market benchmarking, salary surveys, compensation analysis, and cost modeling.
• Develop recommendations for salary structures, incentive plans, and benefits programs based on market trends.
• Ensure internal pay equity and external market competitiveness.
• Support annual salary reviews, bonus planning, and incentive programs.
• Analyze compensation and benefits data to provide actionable insights and recommendations.
• Monitor compensation trends, labor market movements, and regulatory changes.
• Ensure compliance with compensation policies, governance standards, and audit requirements.
• Partner with HR and business leaders to provide expert guidance on compensation, benefits, job evaluation, and recognition programs.
• Prepare reports, dashboards, and presentations using HR analytics and statistical tools.
• Identify opportunities to improve Total Rewards processes, policies, and employee experience.

Requirements
• Bachelor's Degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field.
• Minimum 8 years of overall professional experience.
• At least 5 years of relevant experience in Compensation & Benefits or Total Rewards.
• GCC experience is an advantage.
• Strong expertise in:

Total Rewards
Compensation & Benefits
Job Evaluation
Salary Benchmarking
Market Analysis
Pay Equity
Incentive & Bonus Programs
Benefits Administration
HR Analytics
Cost Modeling
• Advanced analytical and Excel skills with the ability to interpret compensation data.
• Experience working with HRIS systems; SAP ERP Human Resources experience is highly preferred.
• Strong communication, stakeholder management, and project coordination skills.
• Knowledge of employment legislation and compensation governance best practices.

If you are passionate about building competitive and data-driven Total Rewards programs that support organizational success, we encourage you to apply.

Factory 54 is a leading global fashion and lifestyle group, headquartered in Tel Aviv and Amsterdam, with operations across Israel and Europe. As part of the Irani Group, we represent and operate more than 150 of the world's leading luxury fashion, footwear, accessories, and beauty brands.
With over 2,000 employees across the group and approximately 450 professionals at our headquarters, nearly all of our core business activities are managed in-house. Our headquarters brings together experts across Technology, R&D, Digital, E-commerce, Marketing, Finance, Human Resources, Buying, Logistics, Operations, Content, PR, Legal, Construction, and more- working collaboratively to drive innovation, business growth, and exceptional customer experiences.
As one of Israel's leading luxury retailers, Factory 54 continues to grow rapidly, combining fashion, technology, and innovation in a dynamic, fast-paced environment where people make the difference.
Join Our Team
We're looking for a Talent Acquisition & HR Coordinator to join our Recruitment & HR team.
In this role, you'll partner with hiring managers across the organization, lead end-to-end recruitment for a wide variety of corporate positions, and help shape the teams that drive Factory 54's continued growth.
If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, enjoy building meaningful relationships, and are passionate about connecting exceptional talent with exciting career opportunities, we'd love to hear from you.

Key Responsibilities
• Manage full-cycle (end-to-end) recruitment, from role briefing and sourcing through offer stage and onboarding.

• Support employee experience and engagement projects that strengthen our workplace culture.

Requirements
• +2 years of experience managing end-to-end recruitment processes.
• Hands-on experience with LinkedIn Recruiter, sourcing tools, and Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS).
• Ability to manage multiple recruitment processes simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
• Strong interviewing, assessment, and stakeholder management skills.
• Excellent interpersonal and communication abilities with a service-oriented mindset.
• Proactive, business-oriented approach with the ability to work independently and drive recruitment initiatives.
• Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to influence hiring managers and cross-functional stakeholders.
• Passion for talent acquisition and a strong motivation to grow within a leading and rapidly evolving organization.

Why Join Factory 54?
At Factory 54, recruitment is much more than filling positions- it's a strategic driver of our company's growth and success.
Joining our team means you'll have the opportunity to partner with inspiring leaders, recruit across diverse business functions, contribute to impactful HR and Employer Branding projects, and grow your career in an innovative, fast-paced, and collaborative environment.

jobs.title: Senior Compensation Analyst
jobs.description:
Employee Applicant Privacy Notice

Who we are:

Shape a brighter financial future with us.

Together with our members, we’re changing the way people think about and interact with personal finance.

We’re a next-generation financial services company and national bank using innovative, mobile-first technology to help our millions of members reach their goals. The industry is going through an unprecedented transformation, and we’re at the forefront. We’re proud to come to work every day knowing that what we do has a direct impact on people’s lives, with our core values guiding us every step of the way. Join us to invest in yourself, your career, and the financial world.

The role:

As a Senior Compensation Analyst, you will play a key role in shaping SoFi Technologies’ global compensation strategy and programs to attract, retain, and motivate top talent globally. This role will lead our global job architecture, compensation structures, market benchmarking, and broad-based compensation modeling. You will use expert knowledge, market data, trends, technology, and financial analysis to develop compensation frameworks that are competitive, scalable, and aligned with our compensation philosophy.

You will be responsible for developing our annual cash and equity guidelines, modeling program budgets, and partnering with Finance on monthly stock-based compensation forecasting and analysis. You will also support the executive compensation function, working closely with the Executive Compensation Lead on Compensation Committee materials, executive compensation programs, and related disclosures.

What you’ll do:

Broad-Based Strategy & Execution

• Lead global compensation benchmarking, market pricing, and the development of compensation structures, including base salary ranges, target bonuses, and long-term incentive guidelines.
• Own and enhance SoFi’s global job architecture, including job families, career levels, job profiles, and related compensation frameworks.
• Lead job architecture maintenance and redesign projects to support organizational design, workforce planning, career development, and talent acquisition.
• Develop recommendations for annual cash and equity program budgets based on market data, business priorities, affordability, and compensation strategy.
• Develop and maintain equity guidelines and model the share usage, dilution, and stock-based compensation impact of new hire, promotion, refresh, and other equity programs.
• Partner with Finance on monthly stock-based compensation forecasting, variance analysis, and long-term planning.
• Apply country-specific market practices and regulatory considerations to ensure compensation structures are locally competitive while remaining consistent with SoFi’s global compensation philosophy.
• Monitor compensation trends, market practices, and emerging developments, providing recommendations and insights to the Compensation team and business leaders.
• Partner with People, Finance, Legal, Compliance, and Talent Acquisition to ensure compensation programs support business needs and are administered consistently.

Executive Compensation Support

• Support the preparation of quarterly Compensation Committee and Board materials, including executive compensation analyses, scenario modeling, and executive-ready insights.
• Assist with the preparation of proxy disclosures, including the Compensation Discussion and Analysis and SEC-required compensation tables, in partnership with Legal, Accounting, Finance, and Investor Relations.
• Support executive compensation operations, including incentive program tracking, Compensation Committee approval materials, stock ownership policy compliance, and executive offer letter development.
• Conduct executive compensation benchmarking and market analysis using relevant survey and peer company data.

What You'll Need:

• Bachelor’s degree in finance, economics, human resources, business, or a related field. An advanced degree or relevant professional
